handoff.goal: Make the property ready for its next occupant and resolve the departing tenancy's financial relationship, allowing the two outcomes to progress independently.

documents.title: Lease, renewal and September 2026 modification
documents.text:
Residential lease, 142 West 88th Street, Triplex. Landlord: Whitcomb Holdings LLC. Tenants: Laura and Michael Brenner. Signed November 22, 2022. Initial term January 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024. Renewed April 9, 2024 through June 30, 2027. Modified September 2, 2026 to end on September 23, 2026. Security deposit held by landlord: $43,800.
Lease ¶31: Tenant has inspected the apartment and building, states they are in good order and repair, and takes the apartment as-is except for latent defects.
Rider ¶4: Tenant pays one half of the water and gas bills within 30 days of receiving copies from the landlord.
Rider ¶6: Tenant returns the apartment in its original condition, normal wear and tear excepted. Landlord may apply the security deposit to damage.
Rider ¶14: Tenant must inform landlord of any pre-existing damage within two days of occupancy.
Rider ¶39: Landlord permits the tenant's four existing dogs: two small mixed-breed dogs, one bulldog and one miniature dachshund. No additional pets without the landlord's prior permission.
Modification ¶8: Landlord and tenant walk through the apartment for damage within 48 hours of vacancy.

documents.title: Restoration funds
documents.text: Whitcomb Holdings has set aside $65,000 for the move-out restoration of the triplex. This is separate from the Brenners' security deposit.

documents.title: Laura Brenner: apartment condition, June 11, 2024
documents.text:
From: Laura Brenner
To: Eleanor Whitcomb
Date: June 11, 2024
Subject: Apartment condition

Attached are photographs detailing the condition of the screens and other issues in the apartment, all of which were existing upon our arrival. I know you're aware of the terrace, the intercom/doorbell and perhaps others of these as well, but I've included everything that's not strictly cosmetic like the paint and wires. If you have questions about any of this please let me know.

Laura

22 photographs attached.

documents.title: Move-out walk-through, September 24, 2026
documents.text:
Move-out walk-through, September 24, 2026. Present: Eleanor Whitcomb (owner), Michael Brenner (tenant), Karen Liu (broker) and Paul Novak. Eleanor took 60 photographs; Paul recorded a video.
Entrance and stairs: front step chipped; saddle past the vestibule gouged with a broken corner; common-foyer mahogany door with veneer sheared off one section; newel post chipped and gouged; stair carpet edges scraped and torn on several steps; top molding and rail edge damaged between the second and third floors.
Living room: parquet scraped, scratched and gouged; decorative border missing inlay pieces and stained; finish worn through in places.
Dining room: paint blotches, gouges and a large stain on the parquet; damaged parquet corners; antique hearth tiles missing and broken; mahogany mantel damaged; a large piece of the doorway casing damaged or missing.
Office: carpet heavily stained; floor scratched. Mahogany window sills throughout: stains, ring marks and gouges.
West master suite: large dark stains on the plank floor, including in front of the fireplace, with a urine odor; scrapes and gouges; soot staining on the wall, ceiling, mantel and shelving; a deep gouge in the molding.
East master bedroom: ceiling damaged where the period chandeliers were replaced with the tenants' fixtures. East bathroom ceiling stained and damaged.
Third floor: southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing pulled away, with protruding nails and torn wood; not safe to use. Northeast storage-ladder railing scraped. Northeast bedroom plank floor with a dark urine stain; bedroom door broken and the plaster behind it damaged. Bathroom tub porcelain chipped and vanity panel broken. Great-room plank floor heavily stained and gouged with a urine odor; plaster damage and staining down one wall; ceiling damaged around the light fixtures.
Karen Liu also noted odors in several rooms.

documents.title: Westside Plaster & Paint: plaster, paint and woodwork
documents.text: Westside Plaster & Paint: plaster repair and soot cleanup in the great room, northeast bedroom and west master suite: $11,366.67. Restore woodwork and fireplaces: window sills, doorway casing, moldings, mantels, hearth tiles, foyer door veneer and the northeast bedroom door: $10,000. Bathroom repairs and caulking: tub chip repair and vanity panel: $3,762.50. Total $37,912.49. Deposit of $10,000 at start; balance on completion, payable within 14 days. About two weeks on site. documents.title: Feld Architecture: kitchen repair sign-off, August 24, 2026
documents.text: Feld Architecture PLLC to Eleanor Whitcomb, August 24, 2026. Kitchen water repair, 142 West 88th Street: completion and sign-off. The leak under the kitchen sink came from a failed supply line. The plumber replaced both supply lines and shutoff valves; the carpenter replaced the sink base cabinet and patched 6 sq ft of subfloor. A moisture check on August 24 read dry at every point. The repair is complete and signed off; no further work is needed.

documents.title: Owner instructions
documents.text:
From Eleanor Whitcomb, September 25, 2026.
I want the triplex back on the market as soon as possible, ideally showing by late October for a December 1 move-in.
Have Feld Architecture walk the apartment first and give me a condition schedule and a scope with a budget before we commit to repairs. Then line up the trades.
The loft-ladder railing is dangerous. Keep everyone off that ladder until it is fixed.
Feld finished the kitchen water repair in August and signed it off, so there's nothing left to do in the kitchen.
You can approve work within the funds I've set aside; I don't need to sign each contract. Deal with the contractors directly.
I'll settle the Brenners' deposit separately once we know what the damage costs.

documents.title: Condition and maintenance history
documents.text:
Condition and maintenance history, compiled by Eleanor Whitcomb.
Before the tenancy: the apartment was painted and the floors redone in late 2022. Karen Liu's 2022 listing photographs show intact fireplace tiles and window woodwork, and good floors with a few dark spots and one diagonal scratch in the living room. A family stayed briefly over the 2022 holidays before the Brenners moved in on January 9, 2023.
June 11, 2024: Laura Brenner emailed 22 photographs of screens, a loose dining-room hearth, loose or broken tiles, missing molding and a small missing parquet piece, describing them as existing on arrival. None of this was reported within the two days required by rider ¶14.
Complaints during the tenancy: uneven room temperatures, a clogged toilet, a roof leak, weak dryer performance, bin lids and the intercom. Work done: screens repaired, window weather stripping and five temperature sensors added, a new intercom installed and the leaks repaired.
June 2024: during a screen inspection Eleanor found a dog accident on the floor; Laura apologized and cleaned it up.
Repeated indoor grilling caused grease odors and set off smoke alarms. Eleanor asked the Brenners to stop.
August 2026: a slow leak under the kitchen sink damaged the cabinet base and subfloor. Feld Architecture managed the repair: new supply lines and shutoff valves, a replaced sink base and a patched subfloor. Work finished August 21; Feld signed it off on August 24 after a moisture check. No further work is needed.

workPlan.title: Restoration assessment and loft railing safety repair
workPlan.summary: Proceed with Feld Architecture to produce a condition schedule and written repair scope and budget note for the whole triplex, and complete the permanent repair of the unsafe southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing.
workPlan.desiredOutcome: Get a clear, room-by-room scope with quantities so all restoration trades can quote consistently, and eliminate the immediate loft-ladder safety hazard so site visits and subsequent work can proceed safely.
scope: Complete on-site assessment visit of the full triplex and photograph and measure documented deficiencies.
Produce a room-by-room condition and quantity schedule with photographs and measurements.
Provide a written scope of repairs by trade with a preliminary budget note based on the site assessment.
Rebuild and secure the southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing and test it under load so the ladder area is safe to use.
workPlan.rationale: Owner direction is to have Feld Architecture walk the unit first and deliver a condition schedule and scope with budget before committing to broader repairs. Separately, the loft-ladder railing is a documented safety hazard and should be permanently repaired immediately while the unit is empty. Once the assessment report is delivered, we can request quotes from floor restoration, plaster and paint, stair and millwork, and carpet vendors against the same written scope.

selections.scope: Complete on-site assessment visit of the full triplex and photograph and measure documented deficiencies.
selections.reason: Owner wants a full walk-through by Feld before committing to the broader restoration work, and the move-out condition record shows deficiencies across multiple rooms and trades.

selections.scope: Produce a room-by-room condition and quantity schedule with photographs and measurements.
selections.reason: The condition schedule is needed to define quantities so floor, plaster and paint, millwork, and carpet vendors can quote consistently against the same scope.

selections.scope: Provide a written scope of repairs by trade with a preliminary budget note based on the site assessment.
selections.reason: This gives an owner-level budget and a trade-separated scope so we can request apples-to-apples repair quotes and stay aligned with the late October showing target.

selections.reason: The move-out walk-through notes the railing has pulled away with protruding nails and is unsafe; this is an immediate safety issue that should be permanently repaired now while the unit is vacant.

messages.title: Quote request: Loft railing repair
messages.body:
Hello,

Please quote and schedule urgent make-safe repair for the southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing that has pulled away with protruding nails and is unsafe to use. Please confirm the earliest date you can complete a permanent repair, and whether you can provide an earlier temporary make-safe option (for example, securing, removing, or blocking access) until the permanent repair is completed. Access: the unit is empty and Eleanor Whitcomb holds keys; please coordinate a visit time and we will confirm access the day before.

Thanks,
Whitcomb Holdings

Please confirm earliest site visit date and the report delivery timing. Thanks,
Whitcomb Holdings
